text:
marie: ran nightly nsys profile on dedicated pool with batching-v2. kernel time distribution looks odd, matmul up big. posting top-lines

marie: ```
nsys summary (run: nightly-batching-v2)
GPU activities (top by total time):
- matmul_fused_kernel ................ 41.2s (39%)
- attention_fused_forward_kernel ..... 22.8s (21%)
- kv_cache_read_kernel ............... 15.4s (14%)
- softmax_stable_kernel .............. 9.6s (9%)
- small-launch-thin-kernels .......... 6.2s (6%)
- cudaMemcpyAsync (host<->device) ... 4.0s (4%)
others ................................ 6.4s
Total GPU-active time: 105.6s
SM occupancy (top): matmul_fused 55% | attention_fused 36% | small-launch 12%
average SM util across run: 61%
peak concurrent kernels: 3
```

alim: what was the input mix? short vs long sequences and batch packing?

marie: running a 70/30 mix short/long; batching heuristic now tries to pack shorts into one launch — that likely increased large matmuls per launch instead of more balanced smaller ones.

devon: can you paste the nvprof stat for matmul? warp efficiency, inst_issued, regs per thread?

marie: ```
nvprof --analysis-metrics
Kernel: matmul_fused_kernel
Time: 41.2s
Warp Execution Efficiency: 78%
SM Occupancy: 0.55
DRAM Utilization: moderate (memory bound for some kernels)
Issue Stall: 23% (instr issue), Memory Bound: 29%
Registers per thread: 64
Shared Mem per block: 12KB
Active blocks per SM: 4
```

jamal: Warp eff 78% + occupancy 55% = not terrible but combined with larger batch-size means matmul does more total FLOPs. Might be that packing increases GEMM size and we hit a suboptimal kernel variant.

devon: agree. our kernel selector chooses tiling based on M,N,K thresholds. maybe new packing pushed M or N into a tile size that picks the fused matmul kernel instead of the high-occupancy fallback. can we try forcing fallback for that size?

marie: will try forcing fallback compile and re-run nvprof tomorrow. also noticed kv_cache_read is 15s — looks memory bound. prefetch flag was off in this run.

alim: prefetch off? that explains KV cost. enabling prefetch trades extra memcpy overhead but reduces read stalls. worth testing as part of bisect.

perf-bot: automated_regression_check: matmul_fused_kernel total_time +12% compared to baseline (ts=1844000000). Regression flagged: perf_regression_987. See /perfs/1845/regressions/987

devon: ok plan: (1) marie revert batching-v2 -> run (2) devon enable prefetch for KV -> run (3) jamal force kernel-selector fallback / recompile -> run. micro-bisect order as listed. each run: nsys+nvprof+perfetto timeline.

marie: i'll run (1) tonight on dedicated-small pool, post nsys+nvprof snippets here.

devon: i'll take (2) and run with the same input mix, will test prefetch and different cudaMemcpy concurrency.

jamal: I'll prototype a kernel selector rule: if packed_M*N > X then pick high-occupancy kernel. should be quick to validate.

marie: thanks. @devon @jamal cc perf-bot. I'll update thread with results. :thumbsup:

devon: also adding a perfetto capture suggestion: capture timeline around tail latencies to see small-launch overhead spikes — I suspect launch overhead contributes ~6% of GPU time when we have many small kernels.```
